card.title: Refraction at plane surfaces — total internal reflection

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Snell's law bends a ray toward the normal when it enters a slower medium, and the frequency stays the same. Total internal reflection needs the light to be inside the denser medium and past the critical angle, where sin c = n2/n1. For glass of index 1.50 against air, that angle is about 42°.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: For n = 1.50, c is about 42°.  ·  The incident medium must be the denser one.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Snell's law is n1 sin i = n2 sin r, with both angles measured from the normal. The frequency does not change at a stationary boundary. The speed and the wavelength do.  ·  If light enters a slower medium, a larger index, the ray bends toward the normal. If it enters a faster medium, it bends away. A larger index means a smaller speed.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Snell's law  ·  Critical angle  ·  Total internal reflection  ·  Optical fibre

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Refraction at plane surfaces — total internal reflection  ·  Frequency stays the same.  ·  The ray bends toward the normal when it slows.  ·  TIR needs the larger index on the incident side.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Lens maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). Power P = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres); lenses add powers in contact.  ·  Refraction at a plane surface (Snell): n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂. Total internal reflection when θ > θ_c, sinθ_c = n₂/n₁ (n₂<n₁).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Why does a fibre keep the light in?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Glass has n = 1.50. Find sin c for a ray going from glass toward air, and state the approximate critical angle.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: When light enters glass from air it bends → B  ·  TIR can occur when light goes → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Total internal reflection happens only when light is going from the larger index toward the smaller index, and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle. Then there is no refracted ray.  ·  At the critical angle the refracted ray runs along the boundary, so r = 90° and sin c = n2/n1. For glass to air, n2 = 1 and sin c = 1/n.  ·  At exactly the critical angle the light grazes the surface. Beyond it, all the light is reflected. The reflection is stronger than an ordinary glass-to-air reflection at a small angle.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The critical angle is the onset.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ lens maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/r₁ − 1/r₂). power p = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres); lenses add powers in contact..  ·  TIR does not happen when light enters glass from air.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: At the critical angle the ray is along the boundary, not yet fully reflected as the only path in the 'greater than' sense.  ·  Frequency does not fall in glass.  ·  sin c = 1/n for glass to air, not n.
